precedent_checks.what_it_proves: (i) the period image has a functorial (Baily-Borel type) compactification on which the Griffiths bundle extends amply, so the Griffiths bundle is semiample; (ii) the Hodge bundle of a Calabi-Yau VHS is semiample under extra conditions -- a snippet gives them as 'M_X integrable with torsion combinatorial monodromy'; (iii) deduces the Prokhorov-Shokurov b-semiampleness conjecture, verifying (ii)'s conditions geometrically via Ambro and Kollar's minimal lc centres. search-snippet level only (arxiv.org, adsabs, researchgate unreachable from WebFetch: DNS failure); unverified
precedent_checks.does_it_imply_C1: No, as far as can be determined. The Prokhorov-Shokurov conjecture (PS09 Conj. 7.13, as restated in the Floris-Lazic travel guide arXiv:1907.10490) assumes the boundary is effective over the generic point; the Iitaka kappa(F)=0 reduction produces a sub-boundary that is negative on the generic fibre (ORD 01-introduction.tex 'The auxiliary sub-boundary in this formula can be negative on the generic fibre'; ORB introduction.tex:295-297 and reduced-root.tex:236-240: BFMT Thm 6.28 identifies the Hodge divisor with the moduli divisor 'permitting negative coefficients', but Thm 1.5 (semiampleness) needs generic effectiveness). If BFMT's CY-Hodge-bundle theorem applied to the least-index root-cover VHS (i.e. if its integrability/torsion-combinatorial-monodromy conditions could be verified there), M would be semiample, M = p*L with L ample, and C1 would be a trivial corollary (L big => K_S+jL big). Nobody, including BFMT, claims C_{n,m} as a consequence, which is indirect evidence that the conditions are not known in this case. Verdict: BFMT CONTAINS the machinery C1 is built from (Def 2.9 transcendental part, Lemmas 2.16, 5.6, Thm 6.28, the Baily-Borel picture in which boundary strata have lower dimension) but NOT the statement; it neither implies nor contains C1 on current evidence. Residual risk recorded in family_D.falls_to.

candidates.statement: Y smooth projective, V a rationally polarized integral pure VHS on a dense open U whose entire highest Hodge step is a line, M in Pic(Y)_Q with tau*M ~_Q c J (extended highest line) on an alteration. Then after modification there is p:Y->S with connected fibres onto the (normalised) full period image and a nef L with M ~_Q p*L and K_S + jL big for j >> 0. Mechanism: Brunebarbe-Cadorel gives K_S + D big; rational minimality (BFMT transcendental part) + Andre normality + a tangential rank principle (or Ax-Schanuel in ORB) give nu(L|D_i) < nu(L) on every boundary component with N != 0 and every divisor fixed by finite inertia; section counting then removes D.

test2.evidence: Neither S, L nor 'K_S + jL big' occurs in the goal C_{n,m}. In L the closest statements are BC's 'K_S + D big' and Ambro's 'M = h*A, A nef big' (effective case), from which the C1 conclusion follows trivially only under the effective-boundary hypothesis that fails here. The NEED for some positivity of M on the kappa=0 locus is analytic (it is the classical obstruction Birkar names); the specific weakened target (adjoint bigness on the full period image, not semiampleness, not bigness of L) plus the rank-loss lemma that proves it are not subterms of L. Borderline because 'replace an open semiampleness statement by the weakest adjoint statement that Viehweg-type addition can use' is a natural goal-directed reformulation.

BSA does not use it. Removing C1 disconnects the headline theorems of four manuscripts; no alternative path exists in the papers (the alternative ORD proofs Secs. 8-9 re-prove the same rank-loss step).

final.justification: No statement found in any field giving adjoint bigness K_S + jL of a possibly non-big Hodge line on the full period image with boundary and ramification absorbed; BFMT and Ambro give stronger conclusions only under the generic-effectiveness hypothesis that the Iitaka kappa(F)=0 case violates. Every ingredient is named prior art (BC, BBT, BFMT, Andre, Bakker-Tsimerman Ax-Schanuel, CKS, Siu-type volume subtraction): the candidate is their problem-specific coupling, not a transfer. Downgrade risks: (i) an expert shows BFMT's CY-Hodge-bundle conditions hold for root-cover VHS (=> N1 corollary); (ii) a boundary-absorption statement exists in the hyperbolicity literature (Brunebarbe 2020, BFMT Secs. 5-6, 2608.22682: not read in full); (iii) the ~1000-line rank-loss proof is wrong (then the item is void, not merely downgraded); (iv) discoverability arm B hits. Confidence is lower than 322/287 because the claim is extraordinary (settles C_{n,m}) and unreviewed.

family_D.falls_to: D2 if any of: (a) an expert (e.g. Bakker, Filipazzi, Mauri, Tsimerman, Ambro, Fujino, Brunebarbe) shows BFMT's CY-Hodge-bundle semiampleness conditions (integrable, torsion combinatorial monodromy) hold for least-index root-cover VHS of kappa=0 fibres with negative generic sub-boundary, making C1 a corollary; (b) a boundary-absorption statement K + jL big for a lower-rank Hodge line appears in BFMT Secs. 5-6, Brunebarbe 2020 or arXiv:2608.22682 (none read in full); (c) P-C1 arm B shows contamination-controlled models propose the full-period base + rank-loss route at the calibrated rate. The family claims collapse (not merely downgrade) if the ~1000-line rank-loss proof fails.
family_D.not_transfer: Hodge theory -> birational geometry is a known route (Kawamata 1981/85, Viehweg-Zuo, Ambro, BFMT); o-minimality -> moduli part is BFMT's route. P-C1.arm_A_pivot: Give the reduction (relative Iitaka fibration, K ~ g*(K_Y+B+M)+R with B klt, M nef = Hodge line of the least-index root cover, (K_Y+B+M) big on q-fibres) AND the C1 statement; ask for a proof. P-C1.arm_B_decisive: Give the reduction only, plus the instruction 'b-semiampleness of M is unavailable because the generic sub-boundary is negative; find a positivity statement about M that suffices for C_{n,m} and prove it'. Do not mention period images as bases or adjoint bigness. Decides N3.
P-C1.equivalence: Hit: M ~_Q p*L for a morphism p to a base S on which K_S + jL is big (or any statement implying it WITHOUT assuming semiampleness/abundance of M or an effective generic boundary), with a proof sketch whose key step removes the boundary/ramification using lower numerical dimension of L there. Proposals that assume b-semiampleness, abundance of M, or log abundance, or that keep the log boundary (K_S + D + jL big), are misses. Partial credit (recorded, not counted): correct target without a viable rank-loss mechanism.
P-C1.pass_criterion: N3 survives if arm-B pass@256 is below the calibrated threshold.
